project_name: Benchmarking Molecular Descriptors with Actively Identified Subsets (MolDAIS)
summary: This research presents a novel approach called MolDAIS (Molecular Descriptors with Actively Identified Subsets) for molecular property optimization. The method addresses the challenge of optimizing molecules in high-dimensional spaces by using molecular descriptors - sets of rotationally and translationally invariant calculations performed on molecular graphs - coupled with active subspace identification. MolDAIS employs a sparse axis-aligned subspace Gaussian Process prior, which actively learns an encoding while performing Bayesian optimization. Recent works\cite{sorourifar_accelerating_2024,maus_local_2023} are increasingly turning towards active encoding of molecular feature spaces. The researchers evaluated MolDAIS on three case studies: experimental lipophilicity measurements for 4,200 compounds from the MoleculeNet benchmark collection\cite{wu2018moleculenet}, log P optimization over the 250,000-molecule ZINC subset popularized by Kusner et al.\cite{kusner2017grammar}, and computed power conversion efficiencies for 30,000 organic photovoltaic candidates from the Harvard Clean Energy Project\cite{hachmann2011harvard}. In all cases, MolDAIS demonstrated superior performance compared to other optimizers, particularly in larger datasets. For the log P optimization, MolDAIS consistently found the optimal molecule within 100 iterations. The method also showed strong performance in constrained optimization problems, often achieving the best-case scenario and maintaining a favorable worst-case scenario compared to other methods. Overall, MolDAIS proved efficient in identifying high-performing molecules in low-data regimes, offering a promising approach for molecular property optimization tasks.
